key_insight: A cognitively grounded small language model framework can generate more realistic SUD patient dialogue by aligning responses with latent patient states like beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness to change.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support scalable, lower-cost, and more deployable patient-dialogue systems for substance use counseling in privacy- and resource-constrained settings.
method: Detect cognitive components from patient history and counselor questions.
Use knowledge distillation, human-preference optimization, and attention-guided reward shaping to train smaller models.
Generate dialogue with explicit alignment to cognitive states rather than generic fluent responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on automatic metrics (BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR, BLEU) and LLM-as-judge hit metrics versus generic instruction-tuned and domain-specific SLM baselines, with especially strong gains for open-ended cognitive components.
watch_item: Performance is based on abstracted evaluation metrics and model judgments, so real-world clinical reliability, safety, and generalization still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
